name: Open the print dialog
plain: Opens the system print dialog for the page, no click required in most browsers.
meaning: A site can ask to print itself or a hidden frame. It cannot choose a printer or print silently, and it cannot read what the person does in the dialog.

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Sandboxed frames need allow-modals; cross-origin frames print only their own content
steps: afterprint fires when the dialog closes

limits.headline: Can open your print window, without a click in most browsers
limits.user_action: Nothing in most cases. It happens when the page runs a print command, or you tap Print.
can: Open the print dialog for the current page
Format the page for print with its own print styles
Let you save the page as a PDF from the print window
cannot: Print without you pressing Print in the dialog
Pick a printer or change the settings for you
See what printer you use or what your printer is called
Print in the background after you leave the page

story.what_it_is: A page can open your print window, usually without asking.
story.for_you: A receipt or ticket page may open the print box by itself. You can always cancel it. Nothing prints until you confirm.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for receipts, tickets and reports, so you get a clean paper version in one step. Print style sheets also let one page look right on screen and on paper.

use_cases.example: After booking, a boarding pass page opens the print box so you can print it.
A statement page offers a print button with a layout cleaned for paper.
An order confirmation has a Print receipt button.
A school portal prints a certificate or a worksheet.
An online document tool prints a neat version without the toolbars.
A warehouse tool prints shipping labels as soon as an order is packed.

technical_bounds: Blocks the page until the dialog is dismissed in most browsers
Cannot print silently, choose the printer, or read the print result (no kiosk printing without enterprise policy)
Chrome ignores print() in sandboxed iframes lacking allow-modals
Repeated print() calls are not rate limited in the spec; Chrome limits when the tab is in the background
Page cannot read the printed output or the printer list

history.change: Print from sandboxed iframes requires allow-modals
